glossary.Thiazide diuretics: Water tablets acting on the distal tubule; they reduce urate excretion and so raise gout risk.
glossary.Indapamide: A thiazide-like diuretic used for hypertension; can raise serum urate.
glossary.Ethambutol: An anti-tuberculosis antibiotic that reduces urate excretion and can trigger gout.
glossary.Anti-TB treatment: The drug combination used for tuberculosis, usually rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol.
glossary.Purine: A building block of DNA and RNA; its breakdown produces uric acid.
glossary.Purine turnover: The rate at which cells break down and remake purines; high in rapid cell death.
glossary.Venesection: Removing blood from a vein on purpose, used to lower iron in haemochromatosis.
glossary.Metatarsophalangeal joint: The joint between a long foot bone (metatarsal) and the first bone of a toe.
glossary.Distal joints: Joints far from the trunk, such as toes, ankles and fingers.
glossary.Extensor surfaces: The back of a joint that straightens the limb, such as the elbow point.
glossary.X-linked recessive: Inherited via a faulty gene on the X chromosome, so it mainly affects males.
glossary.Erosion: A bite-shaped area of bone lost at a joint margin, seen on X-ray.
glossary.Joint space: The gap between bones on X-ray, filled by cartilage; it narrows when cartilage is lost.
glossary.Serum urate: The level of uric acid in the blood.
glossary.Rhomboid: A slanted box shape, like a squashed rectangle.
glossary.Naproxen: A long-acting NSAID painkiller used for acute gout.
glossary.Diclofenac: An NSAID painkiller; also used in acute gout.
glossary.Peptic bleed: Bleeding from an ulcer in the stomach or duodenum.
glossary.Duodenal ulceration: Ulcers in the first part of the small bowel.
glossary.HFpEF: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a stiff heart that fills poorly but pumps normally.
glossary.Warfarin: An oral anticoagulant; with NSAIDs it raises bleeding risk.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Steroid drugs such as prednisolone that suppress inflammation.
glossary.Dialysis: Machine filtering of the blood when the kidneys have failed.
glossary.Methylprednisolone: A corticosteroid that can be injected into a joint.
glossary.Prophylactic: Given to prevent attacks rather than to treat one.
glossary.Titrated: Dose increased gradually to reach the target effect.
glossary.Initiation: The period when a drug is first started.
glossary.Hypoxanthine: A purine breakdown product turned into xanthine by xanthine oxidase.
glossary.Xanthine: The step before uric acid in purine breakdown.
glossary.Uric acid: The end product of purine breakdown in humans; urate is its salt form.
glossary.Inflammasome: A protein complex inside immune cells that switches on IL-1β release.
glossary.Polymerisation: Joining small units into a long chain, as tubulin forms microtubules.
glossary.Neutrophil: The most common white blood cell; it swarms to acute inflammation.
glossary.Phagocytosis: A cell engulfing particles such as crystals or bacteria.
glossary.Mobilising: Releasing stored urate from tissues back into circulation.
glossary.Flare: A sudden return or worsening of symptoms.
glossary.Precipitation: Crystals coming out of solution when a substance is too concentrated.
glossary.Chronic destructive joint disease: Long-term damage to joints visible on X-ray as erosions and deformity.
